On December 8, 1903, the head of the Smithsonian sent his fifty-thousand-dollar flying machine off a houseboat on the Potomac.

It fell straight into the river.

Nine days later, two brothers who ran a bicycle shop in Ohio flew for twelve seconds.

Case closed? Not quite. In 1914, the Smithsonian had Langley's machine rebuilt and flown, then labelled it the first capable of sustained free flight.

So Orville Wright sent the first airplane in history to a museum in London. It stayed twenty years.

The Smithsonian backed down in 1942. And to bring it home, it signed a contract promising never to credit an earlier machine.
